chapters.1.summary: Nehemiah serves in the Persian fortress of Susa. His brother Hanani arrives with men from Judah. They report that the survivors are in great trouble. Jerusalem’s wall is broken, and its gates are burned. Nehemiah sits down and weeps, fasts, and prays for days. He confesses the sins of Israel, his family, and himself. He recalls God’s promise to gather those who return to him. He asks for favor before the king, whose cupbearer he is.
chapters.1.lds: The Seminary lesson studies Nehemiah’s prayer about Jerusalem. What does he ask before he speaks to the king?
chapters.2.summary: Four months later Nehemiah serves wine to the king with a sad face. The king asks why, and Nehemiah is very afraid. He says his fathers’ city lies in ruins. He prays quickly and asks to be sent to rebuild it. He asks for letters to governors and for timber from the king’s forest. The king grants it and sends officers with him. In Jerusalem he inspects the walls by night. He tells the leaders, and they agree to build despite mockery.
chapters.2.lds: Come, Follow Me studies Nehemiah’s answer to mockery. What preparations support his call to rebuild?
chapters.3.summary: The high priest and his fellow priests rebuild the Sheep Gate. The chapter then moves around the wall section by section. Each group is named with the part it repairs. Goldsmiths, perfume makers, and merchants work beside district rulers. One ruler repairs his section with his daughters. Many people repair the wall opposite their own houses. The men of Tekoa repair two sections. Their nobles, however, refuse to work.
chapters.3.lds: The Seminary lesson connects the repairs with serving God. How do named families share the work?
chapters.4.summary: Sanballat and Tobiah mock the builders and their wall. Nehemiah prays, and the wall rises to half its height. The enemies plot to attack Jerusalem. The people pray and post a guard day and night. Workers grow tired, and neighbors warn of raids ten times. Nehemiah stations families with swords, spears, and bows. Half his men work while half hold weapons. A trumpeter stays beside him, and they work from dawn until the stars appear.
chapters.4.lds: Come, Follow Me studies prayer and work during threats. How do guards and the trumpet help protect workers?
chapters.5.summary: A great outcry rises from the people and their wives against fellow Jews. Some have pledged fields and houses to buy grain in the famine. Some have borrowed to pay the king’s tax. Their children are being sold as servants. Nehemiah is very angry and accuses the nobles of charging interest. He says the community has been buying back Jews sold abroad. The nobles are silent and then promise to restore everything. As governor Nehemiah refuses the food allowance and feeds many at his own cost.
chapters.5.lds: What would stopping these charges change for the families?
chapters.6.summary: The wall is nearly finished, with only the gate doors missing. Sanballat and Geshem invite Nehemiah to a meeting four times, meaning harm. He answers that he is doing a great work and cannot come down. A fifth letter accuses him of planning to be king. A hired prophet urges him to hide inside the temple. Nehemiah refuses and sees the plot. The wall is finished in fifty-two days, and the enemies lose heart. Yet Judah’s nobles keep exchanging letters with Tobiah.
chapters.6.lds: Come, Follow Me studies Nehemiah’s response to attempts to stop him. Why does he refuse the proposed meetings?
chapters.7.summary: The wall is built, and the doors are hung. Nehemiah puts his brother Hanani and a trusted commander over Jerusalem. The gates are to stay shut until the sun is hot. Residents stand guard, each near his own house. The city is wide, but few people live in it. God moves Nehemiah to register the people by families. He finds the record of those who first returned. The list of families, numbers, and gifts follows.
chapters.7.lds: Why do the guards need clear instructions after the wall is built?
chapters.8.summary: In the seventh month all the people gather at the Water Gate. They ask Ezra to bring the book of the law of Moses. He reads from early morning until noon on a wooden platform. Men, women, and all who can understand listen. Levites explain the reading, and the people weep. The leaders tell them not to grieve, since the day is holy. On the second day they read about the Feast of Booths. They build shelters of branches and keep the feast with great joy.
chapters.8.lds: Come, Follow Me studies help with understanding scripture. What do the teachers do after Ezra reads?
chapters.9.summary: On the twenty-fourth day the people fast in sackcloth. They read the law for a quarter of the day and confess for another quarter. The Levites lead a long prayer. It recalls creation, Abraham, Egypt, the sea, Sinai, and the manna. It admits that the fathers rebelled again and again. Each time God was merciful and did not abandon them. The prayer says God has been just and the people have done wrong. They are servants in their own land, so they make a written agreement.
chapters.9.lds: The people recall mercy during repeated failure. How does this shape their new promises?
chapters.10.summary: The agreement is sealed by Nehemiah, the priests, the Levites, and the leaders. The rest of the people join with an oath. They will not marry their children to the peoples of the land. They will not buy on the Sabbath, and they will cancel debts every seventh year. Each will pay a yearly sum for the temple’s service. They cast lots for bringing wood to the altar. They promise firstfruits and tithes for the priests and Levites. They say they will not neglect the house of their God.
chapters.10.lds: The Seminary overview studies promises about marriage and Sabbath rest. What supplies do the families also promise?
chapters.11.summary: The leaders live in Jerusalem. The other people cast lots to bring one family in ten into the city. The other nine stay in their towns. The people bless those who volunteer to move. The chapter lists the families of Judah and Benjamin who settle there. It lists priests, Levites, gatekeepers, and singers. An official at the king’s side handles the people’s affairs. The villages of Judah and Benjamin are named last.
chapters.11.lds: Who keeps daily temple service possible while families settle in different towns?
chapters.12.summary: The chapter lists the priests and Levites from the first return onward. For the wall’s dedication the Levites and singers are gathered from their villages. Priests and Levites purify themselves, the people, the gates, and the wall. Two large choirs walk along the top of the wall in opposite directions. Ezra leads one, and Nehemiah follows the other. They meet at the temple and sing loudly. The people offer great sacrifices and rejoice. Men are appointed that day over the storerooms for offerings.
chapters.12.lds: How do the women and children join the public thanks?
chapters.13.summary: The law is read, and the people separate from foreigners. Nehemiah has been away at the king’s court. On his return he finds Tobiah in a temple storeroom and throws him out. The Levites have not been paid and have gone back to their fields. Traders are selling on the Sabbath, so he shuts the gates. Jews have married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. He rebukes them harshly and drives out a priest’s son. He ends by asking God to remember him for good.
chapters.13.lds: The Seminary overview emphasizes Sabbath rest and keeping promises to God. How do Nehemiah’s actions affect workers and families?
